# `Q-22-5` — Unbalanced Brace In Math

> A `{` in a math expression is never closed, or a `}` has no matching `{`.

## What this means

Braces group arguments and sub-expressions. An unclosed `{` is closed at the end of the expression, which usually swallows more than intended; a stray `}` has nothing to close. Either way the intended structure is unknown, so the expression is reported and emitted verbatim in formats that need a conversion.

## Why this happens

Common causes: a missing `}` after editing an argument, an escaped brace typed as a plain one (`\{ x }` when `\{ x \}` was meant), or a `}` left behind after removing a group.

## How to fix it

Balance the braces. To typeset a literal brace, write `\{` and `\}`.

## Where it is reported

Math diagnostics point into the `.qmd` at the exact characters inside the
`$…$` or `$$…$$` block, including math that spans several lines or sits
inside a block quote or list item. When a `\newcommand` macro is involved,
a problem inside the macro body points at the definition and a problem in
a macro argument points at the use.
